examples.trans: I understand well (usually).
Today is a (usually) busy day.
Did you hear about this female?
I was busy today because of female.
Did you hear about this hammering too?
I was busy today because of hammering too.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I cannot swim.
I couldn't contact you because I was busy.
Did you hear about this fluorescent light too?
I was busy today because of fluorescent light too.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.
I want to replace, you know right now.
How about trying to replace, you know together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Kinship term used by females.

meanings.en: older male friend or colleague (used by a female)
meanings.note: Commonly used in Korea to address a close older male acquaintance or coworker.

examples.trans: I have one older brother.
Oppa, do you have time right now?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken contraction of 이것.

examples.trans: How much is this?
Please look at this.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used for giving things to someone of equal or lower status.

examples.trans: I gave a gift.
Please give me some water.

이러다.gloss: to do this, to act like this

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this
meanings.note: Contracted from 이러하다.

examples.trans: Why are you acting like this?
Please don't do this.
Did you hear about this man?
I was busy today because of man.

meanings.note: 르-irregular verb; conjugates as 불러요 in polite present, but 부르면 in conditional.
Used with 노래 ('song'): 노래를 부르다.

examples.trans: The team leader called you to the conference room.
Please call my name loudly.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.
Did you hear about this youth?
I was busy today because of youth.
Did you hear about this dating, romance?
I was busy today because of dating, romance.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Describes something unusual or out of the ordinary.
Used when sensing something is wrong.

examples.trans: The computer sounds a bit strange.
It's suspicious that he's suddenly being so nice.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem adjective: 바쁘다 + -아요 becomes 바빠요.

examples.trans: Work at the company is so busy these days.
If you're busy, please contact me later.
Did you hear about this jam?
I was busy today because of jam.
Did you hear about this lid too?
I was busy today because of lid too.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.
I want to open, so right now.
How about trying to open, so together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.
I want to let's break up right now.
How about trying to let's break up together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.
Did you hear about this since I intend to?
I was busy today because of since I intend to.

meanings.note: verb do well

examples.trans: Study well.
You did well.
Did you hear about this someone else's?
I was busy today because of someone else's.
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.
I want to staying as a freeloader right now.
How about trying to staying as a freeloader together tomorrow?

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: Did you hear about this in private life?
I was busy today because of in private life.
Let's meddle together today.
I worked hard to meddle yesterday too.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
